(line 1620) plainly. The person's meaning is kept whole: only these words are re-said, as "its living going on with possibling and discovering" and "within". Also confirmed: the spiral of one with prior − has next priors +, +, −, −, +, +, −, − over 8 steps and 10 shares +, 0, −, 0, its (prior, next) forms (−,+), (+,+), (+,−), (−,−), two changing and two not; the code holds no word *universal*; both quoted sentences stand word for word once each in Natural_Intelligence_v391.md, lines 36 and 1628.

fixed.sentence: A parity's two directions are + and −.
fixed.text: A parity's two directions are + and −, universal-parity and other-parity. A self has two parities only, universal-parity and other-parity, and no other parity resolves with a same-existing-society. A 0 is no third parity: a 0 is a me, the between of universal-parity and other-parity, within a self or within a bi-coupling, a new self. The living 0 lives between other-parity and universal-parity, its living going on with possibling and discovering, aiming forward, within the living self. Each momentarying a living self changes from its now parity to the opposite next parity, or does not change. With Exhibit ONE's code, a self's own parity, its next prior with 11-next-co-observing, is + or − at each case of one sharing with a prior + or −, with none to three parities received; with no prior it is + or − with one parity or agreeing parities received, and an empty set with none, only 0s or parities parting received; it is 0 at none. A 0 stands only as a between: 12's 0, prior and now agreeing; 14's 0, parities parting; and a 0 a self shares with 10, with its prior same-existing, prior and now agreeing, and at a first sharing, parities parting, its next prior an empty set. A spiral of one with prior − goes +, +, −, −, its now and next parities at four joint forms, two changing and two not changing. The code holds no naming of which sign is universal-parity and which other-parity: "As signs, + and − are alike." Both sides stand: the two directions named universal-parity and other-parity at this sentence, or the sentence as it stands.
